name: application-gantt-bar-chart
title: Gantt Bar Chart
description: Horizontal project timeline with task bars positioned on a day/week grid, dependency arrows between tasks, milestone diamond markers, and a vertical today-line.
useWhen: Visualizing a project schedule where tasks have a start date and duration across a shared time axis.
You need to show dependencies between tasks (task B can't start until task A finishes).
Milestones (zero-duration events like a launch date) need to appear alongside duration-based tasks.
avoidWhen: You only need a simple ordered sequence of steps with no dates — use Steps or Stepper Wizard instead.
The timeline is a single-track log or media scrubber rather than multiple parallel task rows — use Timeline Scrubber instead.
You need heavy interactivity (drag-to-resize, drag-to-reschedule) — this is a static/display-only chart; wire your own drag handling on top of the bar positions.
responsiveBehavior: The grid columns are proportional (CSS grid fractions), so the chart compresses smoothly down to its task-name column's minimum width; below that, wrap the chart in a horizontally scrolling container.
accessibility: Milestone markers include visually hidden (sr-only) text describing the milestone since the diamond shape conveys no information to assistive technology.
Dependency arrows and the today-line are aria-hidden decorative overlays; the underlying task list order and labels carry the real information.
Bar color alone does not distinguish tasks — each bar also carries its task label as visible text.

variants.title: Gantt Bar Chart
variants.description: A 10-day grid with four tasks: Research and Design connected by a dependency arrow, a Build bar, a Launch milestone diamond, and a today-line crossing Saturday.
accessibility: Each task bar's visible label is the primary way its purpose is conveyed, not its color or position alone.

variants.title: Gantt Bar Chart (Dark)
variants.description: The same 10-day, four-task schedule adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Grid lines, bar colors, and the today-line all remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
